source_text: Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος τῷ Χαρίτωνι εἶπεν· Ἔτι καὶ σὺ εἰπέ, Χάριτον, Χριστιανὸς εἶ; Χαρίτων εἶπε· Χριστιανός εἰμι θεοῦ κελεύσει. Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος πρὸς τὴν Χαριτὼ εἶπε· Σὺ τί λέγεις, Χαριτοῖ; Χαριτὼ εἶπε· Χριστιανή εἰμι τῇ τοῦ θεοῦ δωρεᾷ. Ῥουστικὸς εἶπε τῷ Εὐελπίστῳ· Σὺ δὲ τίς εἶ; Εὐέλπιστος, δοῦλος Καίσαρος, ἀπεκρίνατο· Κἀγὼ Χριστιανός εἰμι, ἐλευθερωθεὶς ὑπὸ Χριστοῦ, καὶ τῆς αὐτῆς ἐλπίδος μετέχω χάριτι Χριστοῦ. Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος τῷ Ἱέρακι εἶπε· Καὶ σὺ Χριστιανὸς εἶ; Ἱέραξ εἶπεν· Ναί, Χριστιανός εἰμι· τὸν γὰρ αὐτὸν θεὸν σέβομαι καὶ προσκυνῶ. Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος εἶπεν· Ἰουστῖνος ὑμᾶς ἐποίησε Χριστιανούς; Ἱέραξ εἶπεν· Ἤμην Χριστιανὸς καὶ ἔσομαι. Παίων δὲ ἑστὼς εἶπε· Κἀγὼ Χριστιανός εἰμι. Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος εἶπε· Τίς ὁ διδάξας σε; Παίων εἶπεν· Ἀπὸ τῶν γονέων παρειλήφαμεν τὴν καλὴν ταύτην ὁμολογίαν. Εὐέλπιστος εἶπεν· Ἰουστίνου μὲν ἡδέως ἤκουον τῶν λόγων, παρὰ τῶν γονέων δὲ κἀγὼ παρείληφα Χριστιανὸς εἶναι. Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος εἶπε· Ποῦ εἰσιν οἱ γονεῖς σου; Εὐέλπιστος εἶπεν· Ἐν τῇ Καππαδοκίᾳ. Ῥουστικὸς τῷ Ἱέρακι λέγει· Οἱ σοὶ γονεῖς ποῦ εἰσιν; Ὁ δὲ ἀπεκρίνατο λέγων· Ὁ ἀληθινὸς ἡμῶν πατήρ ἐστιν ὁ Χριστός, καὶ μήτηρ ἡ εἰς αὐτὸν πίστις· οἱ δὲ ἐπίγειοί μου γονεῖς ἐτελεύτησαν, καὶ ἐγὼ ἀπὸ Ἰκονίου τῆς Φρυγίας ἀποσπασθεὶς ἐνθάδε ἐλήλυθα. Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος εἶπε Λιβεριανῷ· Τί καὶ σὺ λέγεις; Χριστιανὸς εἶ, οὐδὲ σὺ εὐσεβεῖς; Λιβεριανὸς εἶπε· Κἀγὼ Χριστιανός εἰμι· εὐσεβῶ γὰρ καὶ προσκυνῶ τὸν μόνον ἀληθινὸν θεόν.
orientation: After Justin confesses, Rusticus the prefect questions each companion in turn about being Christian.
pass_a_gloss: Rusticus prefect to the Chariton said: Still also you say!, Chariton, Christian you are? Chariton he said: Christian I am of God by command. Rusticus prefect toward the Charito said: You what you say, Charito? Charito she said: Christian I am by the of the God gift. Rusticus he said to the Euelpistus: You but who you are? Euelpistus, slave of Caesar, he answered: Also I Christian I am, having been freed by Christ, and of the same hope I share by grace of Christ. Rusticus prefect to the Hierax said: Also you Christian you are? Hierax he said: Yes, Christian I am; the for same God I revere and I worship. Rusticus prefect said: Justin you he made Christians? Hierax he said: I was Christian and I will be. Paion but having stood he said: Also I Christian I am. Rusticus prefect said: Who [is] the [one] having taught you? Paion he said: From the parents we have received the good this confession. Euelpistus he said: Of Justin on one hand gladly I was hearing of the words, from the parents on other hand also I have received Christian to be. Rusticus prefect said: Where are the parents of you? Euelpistus he said: In the Cappadocia. Rusticus to the Hierax says: The of you parents where are? The but he answered saying: The true of us father is the Christ, and mother [is] the into him faith; the but earthly of me parents they died, and I from Iconium of Phrygia having been torn away hither I have come. Rusticus prefect said to Liberianus: What also you you say? Christian you are, and not you you revere? Liberianus he said: Also I Christian I am; I revere for and I worship the only true God.

lemmas.gloss: command, order here: by God's command
set free here: freed by Christ
share in here: share in the same hope
revere here paired with worship of God
worship here: bow in worship to God
received here: received confession from parents
confession here: open I am a Christian
torn away here: taken away from Iconium
practice true worship toward the true God

choices.why: brief glossary fixes this term for open loyalty to Christ confessed before a judge
brief glossary fixes logos in Justin's school context as teaching, not single word
brief glossary fixes homologia as open I am a Christian declaration received from parents
brief glossary fixes eusebeia as right worship toward the true God incompatible with sacrificing

pass_b_english: Rusticus the prefect said to Chariton, “You as well, Chariton — tell me, are you a Christian?” Chariton said, “I am a Christian by God’s command.” Rusticus the prefect said to Charito, “What do you say, Charito?” Charito said, “I am a Christian by God’s gift.” Rusticus said to Euelpistus, “And who are you?” Euelpistus, a slave of Caesar, answered, “I too am a Christian. I was freed by Christ, and I share in the same hope by Christ’s grace.”

Rusticus the prefect said to Hierax, “Are you also a Christian?” Hierax said, “Yes, I am a Christian. I revere and worship the same God.” Rusticus the prefect said, “Did Justin make you Christians?” Hierax said, “I was a Christian, and I will be one.” Paeon, who stood by, said, “I too am a Christian.” Rusticus the prefect said, “Who taught you?” Paeon said, “We received this good confession from our parents.” Euelpistus said, “I gladly listened to Justin’s teachings, but I too received being a Christian from my parents.” Rusticus the prefect said, “Where are your parents?” Euelpistus said, “In Cappadocia.”

Rusticus said to Hierax, “Where are your parents?” He answered, “Our true father is Christ, and our mother is faith in him. My earthly parents have died. I was torn away from Iconium in Phrygia and have come here.” Rusticus the prefect said to Liberianus, “And what do you say? Are you a Christian? Do you not practice true worship either?” Liberianus said, “I too am a Christian. I practice true worship and worship the only true God.”
